subject: Archaeology
title: Proto-Elamite: The Forgotten Script
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Proto-Elamite: The Forgotten Script.

hook.text: One of the world's oldest writing systems — Proto-Elamite from Iran — was used for only 200 years and then abandoned.

buildup.text: Proto-Elamite appeared around 3000 BCE in southwestern Iran. About 1,600 tablets survive, mostly accounting records.

discovery.text: The numbers can be read — they are similar to Mesopotamian systems. The signs next to the numbers remain a mystery.

twist.text: Many tablets contain errors — as if scribes were not fully trained.

climax.text: Oxford's CDLI project has put high-resolution images online, inviting anyone to try cracking it.

punchline.text: They invented writing, got confused by their own system.

quiz.question: Why was Proto-Elamite possibly abandoned?
options: A conquering army banned all writing in the region
The system may have been too complex — tablets show scribal errors suggesting poor training
A new religion declared writing to be sacrilegious
